A1.justification: Both PDFs contain the same GATEAU research work, with all 31 pages and Appendices A–J available. Text and rendered-page comparisons establish matching scientific content, including equations, tables and figures.

before.justification: v5 reports original GATEAU experiments on LongBench, LongBench-Chat and MT-Bench, alongside ablations, human evaluation and additional appendix experiments.

after.justification: v6 retains these original experimental outcomes, including the benchmark results, human evaluation and appendix analyses.

M1.justification: Section 2 retains identical HMG and CAM components, their weighted sample-selection score and the supervised fine-tuning objective. The appendix method variants also match.

E1.justification: Both versions use LongAlign, ShareGPT and the appendix LongAlpaca experiment. LongBench, LongBench-Chat, MT-Bench, needle retrieval and OOD case-study coverage are unchanged.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain w/o SFT, w/o Long SFT, Full-100%, Perplexity Guidance, CaR and Cherry Selection. Comparator membership also matches throughout the appendix experiments.

E3.justification: Section 3.1 and Appendices A–C retain the same data proportions, model configurations, training budgets, truncation rules, evaluation metrics and judge prompts. Supplementary testing procedures are also unchanged.

E4.justification: The component ablations, sample-characteristic and context-length analyses, needle retrieval tests, hyperparameter studies, diversity and mixed-quality analyses, and case studies are identical in both versions.

E5.justification: Both report averaging two GPT-4 ratings in Section 3.1 and Appendix D. There are no changes to repeated-evaluation counts, seed information or uncertainty-reporting practices.

E6.justification: Numerical results and qualitative findings match throughout the main text and appendices. For example, Table 1 retains GATEAU-LLaMA-10% real-world scores of 55.4 on LongBench-Chat and 58.6 on MT-Bench.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(7), including the HMP and CAS definitions, selection score and training loss, are identical. No mathematical definitions, assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims about selecting samples rich in long-range dependencies and improving alignment using selected subsets.

C2.justification: Result interpretations and Appendix I discussions are identical. The limitations still concern homologous-model availability, targeted capability improvement and base-model context-window limits.

D1.justification: Hardware, hyperparameters, evaluator versions, prompts and execution details remain unchanged. Page 1 retains the same repository link and statement that data, code and models will be available.

R1.justification: Section 4, the bibliography and in-text citations are identical. Positioning relative to prior long-context alignment and short-instruction data-selection research is unchanged.

P1.justification: The arXiv margin stamp changes from v5 dated 21 May 2025 to v6 dated 30 July 2025, and embedded bibliographic metadata is updated. Paper prose, title, author text and section organization are unchanged.

P2.justification: All 15 tables and 18 figures retain their content, captions, formatting and placement. Rendered pages 2–31 are pixel-identical; page 1 differs only in the version/date stamp text.

improvement.justification: v6 preserves the methods, evidence, explanations, limitations and reproducibility information of v5 throughout the main paper and appendices. The updated arXiv stamp, its hyperlink and PDF metadata do not meaningfully change the paper's overall quality.
